The older end of the birth window rests on John's marriage by the later 1620s, the bound carried on the first-wife finding in the marriages unit (from daughter Mary's 1647 Braintree marriage).
The first-wife-Mary finding is one strand of the shared matching-criteria profile.

sources.alignmentNote: Names John's first wife Mary and treats her maiden name as unknown - the compiled-genealogy source of the forename, which the primary Braintree death record ('the wife of John') does not give.
Torrey's first-wife entry ('John (-1663) & 1/wf ? (-1661), b 1628, Weymouth') corroborates a first wife who died 1661 and a marriage before 1628, but leaves her unnamed.

statement: John Gurney's first wife bore the name Mary in the compiled Braintree genealogy (Sprague, p. 695); the primary Braintree town record and Torrey both leave her unnamed - the death record enters only 'the wife of John' - and the 'Mary Richards' of later derivative trees is untraced to any primary record. He married her in England by the mid-1620s, bounded by their daughter Mary Gurney's 1647 Braintree marriage to Daniel Shed (baptized Finchingfield, Essex, 1620), which places the daughter's birth by c. 1628. By every indication she was the mother of his children, though no birth record survives to establish the maternity of any of them. She died at Braintree on 20 September 1661.
